stories.headline: KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun's China Visit Triggers Cross-Strait and Domestic Political Storm
stories.summary: KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun's April 7–12 visit to mainland China — the first by a sitting KMT chair since 2016 — including a meeting with Xi Jinping on April 10, sparked sustained domestic and international commentary. Fallout included civic group calls for investigation of Cheng for alleged CCP collusion, a dispute over whether the Taiwan Foundation for Democracy (funded by MoFA) reimbursed KMT travel costs, Taiwan's government insisting it should lead cross-strait engagement rather than the opposition party, and President Lai publicly rejecting a 'peace through unification' framework at a DPP Central Executive Committee meeting on April 15.

stories.headline: TSMC Posts Record Q1 2026 Profit of 58%, Raises Guidance and Expands 3nm Capacity Globally
stories.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported a 58% year-on-year jump in Q1 2026 net profit (NT$572.48 billion), its fourth consecutive quarter of record earnings, driven by AI chip demand from Nvidia, Apple and others. Chairman C.C. Wei raised full-year revenue growth guidance to above 30% in USD terms, lifted the 2026 capex target to the high end of US$52–56 billion, and announced accelerated 3nm capacity expansion across Taiwan, the US (Arizona), and Japan (Kumamoto). The earnings call also addressed Tesla's competing Terafab chip project recruiting Taiwan engineers, Musk's social media mix-up tagging a different Taiwanese firm, and TSMC's first 2nm mass production entry.

stories.headline: US Senators Reassure Taiwan on Weapons Approvals; Lai Calls for Urgent Special Defense Budget
stories.summary: A bipartisan group of US senators sent a letter to Taiwanese lawmakers assuring them that pending US weapons sales would likely be approved within weeks, while also urging Taipei to accelerate its stalled special defense budget. President Lai separately called for swift passage of the NT$1.25 trillion special defense budget during an inspection of the Army Infantry Training Command in Kaohsiung on April 17, and the National Security Bureau announced it will for the first time directly support military operations during the 2026 Han Kuang exercises.

stories.headline: President Lai Plans Visit to Eswatini, Taiwan's Last African Diplomatic Ally
stories.summary: Taiwan's Presidential Office announced on April 13 that President Lai Ching-te will visit Eswatini from April 22–26 for King Mswati's 40-year coronation anniversary celebration, marking Lai's second overseas trip since taking office. The NSB Director-General traveled in advance to deliver a message to the king. The visit draws attention to Taiwan's shrinking formal diplomatic footprint, with Eswatini its only remaining African ally.

stories.headline: China Documented Amplifying Taiwanese Opposition Voices in Information War Against Lai Government
stories.summary: A Reuters investigation published April 17 documented how Chinese state media outlets, including a CCP-run account on Douyin, are systematically amplifying Taiwanese critics of the DPP — including KMT politicians and social media influencers — to delegitimize President Lai and portray him as inviting Chinese aggression. The report traced the information operation to Chinese warship drills in December 2025 and described multi-platform coordination across Douyin, Facebook, YouTube and TikTok.

stories.headline: Legislature Breaks Budget Gridlock; KMT Demands Briefing on Indian Worker Recruitment Plan
stories.summary: After more than six months of impasse, Taiwan's legislative caucuses from KMT, TPP, and DPP agreed on April 18 to begin reviewing the fiscal year 2026 general budget, pending Premier Cho's appearance. Separately, the KMT caucus on April 17–18 tabled motions demanding that Premier Cho Jung-tai and relevant ministers brief the legislature on the government's plan to recruit Indian migrant workers, raising concerns about social security and labor market impacts.

stories.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported on multiple days this week detecting PLA aircraft and PLAN vessels operating around the island, including 5 PLA aircraft and 6 naval vessels on one day (with 4 entering the southwestern ADIZ) and 7 PLAN vessels and 3 official ships on another day with no aircraft detected. ROC Armed Forces monitored and responded to each instance.

stories.headline: Alleged Tracking Device on KMT Vice Chairman's Car Sparks Political Accusations
stories.summary: A Storm Media report published around April 16 alleged a tracking device had been placed on the vehicle of KMT Vice Chairman and Secretary-General Lee Chien-lung without his knowledge. KMT figures alleged government surveillance ('political surveillance'); Lee himself downplayed the incident and declined to file a police report. New Taipei police said they would meet with Lee to obtain information; the DPP and other officials called for a formal complaint and investigation.

stories.headline: Beijing Expels New York Times Correspondent Over President Lai's DealBook Summit Appearance
stories.summary: Beijing denied a visa renewal to New York Times correspondent Vivian Wang, effectively expelling her from China, in retaliation for President Lai Ching-te's virtual appearance at the NYT DealBook Summit in December 2025. Press freedom organizations described the action as 'visa blackmail.' The move is the latest instance of China using journalist access as diplomatic leverage against Taiwan-related coverage.

stories.headline: Premier Cho Files Protest Over Brazilian Envoy's Remark That Taiwan Is Part of China
stories.summary: Premier Cho Jung-tai said on April 14 that the government would lodge necessary protests after Brazil's envoy stated in an interview that he agreed with Beijing that Taiwan is part of China. Cho said he would use the Santos remarks to assert internationally that Taiwan is not part of China, noting Taiwan and Brazil do not have official diplomatic relations.

stories.headline: War-Game Book Excerpt and Commentary Assess US Military Planning for Taiwan Conflict
stories.summary: A new book excerpt published by Breaking Defense, 'War Plan Taiwan' by Rowan Allport, detailed the history of US military planning for a potential China-Taiwan conflict. The piece was published this week alongside other commentary on Chinese military build-up timelines, the 2027 readiness narrative, and changing US threat assessments.
